done_when: After a sync or an upgrade, a client repo's app-baseline skill keeps the screen on a background refresh and names the open tab of a detail page in its URL rule, in both its Claude and Codex copies, and a test pins that text.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a client creates a repo or upgrades one that already has app-baseline skills from an earlier release.
The helper at line 18 copies an earlier-adoption fixture with no app-baseline files and runs sync before returning (`tests/test_score_notes.py:35-44`). The test then syncs a second time and checks already-current files. The package test also deletes both copies before syncing (`tests/test_fix_app_baseline.py:43-45`). A regression that creates missing skills but fails to replace older copies would pass these proofs while upgraded clients retained the old guidance. The helper also syncs after init before the assertions, masking an init-only omission. Check the new repo immediately after init and an earlier repo with stale copies immediately after its update.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_baseline_keeps_the_screen_on_a_background_refresh

why: On a background refresh, client apps show the loading state again or rebuild the list, so the reader loses scroll position, open sections, selection, focus and typed text.
